title: Mastery Challenge: Angle Systems, Gons, Mils & Polygons

questions.promptText: How many gons (or grads) are equivalent to a standard right angle ($90^\circ$)?
questions.explanation: Since one full revolution is $400\text{ gons}$, a right angle ($1/4$ circle) is $\frac{400}{4} = 100\text{ gons}$.

questions.promptText: Convert an angle of $1600\text{ mils}$ into degrees.
questions.explanation:
$1600 \times \frac{360^\circ}{6400} = 1600 \times \frac{90^\circ}{1600} = 90^\circ$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{1600}{6400} = \frac{1}{4} \text{ rev} = 90^\circ$.

questions.promptText: What is the measure of each interior angle in a regular octagon ($8$-sided polygon)?
questions.explanation:
$\theta = \frac{(8 - 2)180^\circ}{8} = \frac{6 \times 180^\circ}{8} = 135^\circ$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $180^\circ - \frac{360^\circ}{8} = 180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ$.

questions.promptText: What is a 100-sided polygon formally named in geometric taxonomy?
questions.explanation: A polygon with 100 sides is named a hectagon (from Greek *hekaton*, meaning hundred).

questions.promptText: If two straight lines intersect, forming two pairs of vertical angles, and one angle measures $68^\circ$, what is the measure of its adjacent supplementary angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles along a straight intersecting line are supplementary: $180^\circ - 68^\circ = 112^\circ$.

questions.promptText: What is the total sum of the interior angles of a convex hexagon ($n = 6$)?
questions.explanation:
$S = (n - 2) \times 180^\circ = (6 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 4 \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $4 \times 180 = 720^\circ$.

questions.promptText: Which ancient civilization developed the $360$-degree sexagesimal angular system over 4,000 years ago?
questions.explanation: The Babylonians established the 360-degree circle based on base-60 sexagesimal arithmetic and astronomical calendars.

questions.promptText: What is the formal geometric name of an $11$-sided polygon?
questions.explanation: An 11-sided polygon is termed an undecagon (Latin) or hendecagon (Greek).

questions.promptText: Convert an angle of $270^\circ$ into gons (grads).
questions.explanation:
$\text{Gons} = 270^\circ \times \frac{400}{360^\circ} = 270 \times \frac{10}{9} = 300\text{ gons}$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{3}{4} \times 400 = 300\text{ gons}$.

questions.promptText: How many sides does a regular polygon have if each of its interior angles measures $150^\circ$?
questions.explanation:
Exterior angle $= 180^\circ - 150^\circ = 30^\circ$. Number of sides $n = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} = 12$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{360}{180 - 150} = \frac{360}{30} = 12$.

questions.promptText: What is the sum of the EXTERIOR angles of any convex $n$-sided polygon?
questions.explanation: For any convex polygon of any number of sides $n$, traversing the perimeter turns a complete $360^\circ$ full revolution.

questions.promptText: Convert an angle of $4800\text{ mils}$ into radians.
questions.explanation: $\text{Radians} = 2\pi \times \frac{4800}{6400} = 2\pi \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{2}\text{ rad} \approx 4.7124\text{ rad}$.

questions.promptText: What is a polygon with $1,000,000$ ($10^6$) sides called?
questions.explanation: A $10^6$-sided polygon is named a megagon (a myriagon has 10,000 sides; a googolgon has $10^{100}$ sides).

questions.promptText: What is the interior angle of a regular heptagon ($7$-sided polygon)?
questions.explanation:
$\theta = \frac{(7 - 2)180^\circ}{7} = \frac{900^\circ}{7} \approx 128.5714^\circ$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{900}{7} \approx 128.57^\circ$.

questions.promptText: In surveying and aircraft navigation, what is the centesimal minute equal to?
questions.explanation: In the French centesimal system, $1\text{ gon} = 100\text{ centesimal minutes} = 10,000\text{ centesimal seconds}$.

questions.promptText: If the interior angle of a regular polygon is 5 times its exterior angle, how many sides does it have?
questions.explanation:
Interior + Exterior $= 180^\circ \implies 5x + x = 180^\circ \implies 6x = 180^\circ \implies x = 30^\circ$. Number of sides $n = 360 / 30 = 12$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $n = 2 \times (5 + 1) = 12$.

questions.promptText: What distinguishes an equiangular polygon from a regular polygon?
questions.choiceA: An equiangular polygon only requires equal angles, while a regular polygon requires both equal angles AND equal side lengths
questions.choiceB: An equiangular polygon must have an odd number of sides
questions.choiceC: An equiangular polygon is always convex
questions.explanation: A rectangle is equiangular (all $90^\circ$) but not regular unless its sides are also equal (a square).

questions.promptText: Convert an angle of $50\text{ gons}$ into angular mils.
questions.explanation:
$\text{Mils} = 50 \times \frac{6400}{400} = 50 \times 16 = 800\text{ mils}$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $50 \times 16 = 800\text{ mils}$.

questions.promptText: What is the interior angle of a regular Hectagon ($n = 100$)?
questions.explanation:
Exterior angle $= 360^\circ / 100 = 3.6^\circ$. Interior angle $= 180^\circ - 3.6^\circ = 176.4^\circ$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $180 - 3.6 = 176.4^\circ$.

questions.promptText: If a polygon has $n$ vertices, how many triangles can be formed by drawing all non-intersecting diagonals from a single vertex?
questions.explanation: Triangulating a convex $n$-gon from a single vertex divides the polygon into exactly $n - 2$ triangles, giving total angle sum $(n - 2)180^\circ$.

questions.promptText: Convert $3200\text{ mils}$ into gons.
questions.explanation: $3200 \times \frac{400}{6400} = 3200 \times \frac{1}{16} = 200\text{ gons}$ (half a circle / straight angle).

questions.promptText: What is the Greek word origin of "polygon" and its literal translation?
questions.explanation: Polygon is derived from Greek poly (many) and gonia (angles).
